title: A domain-specific language can give agents less room to fail
friendlyTitle: Give an AI agent a small language for its job
summary: Modeloptic argues that complex agents become more dependable when they operate through a small domain-specific language rather than manipulating low-level systems directly. Its financial-modeling example replaces a long sequence of spreadsheet decisions with one structured operation, leaving deterministic formatting and formula work to conventional code.
friendlySummary: Instead of letting an agent control every small detail, give it a few clear actions made for the task. Normal software can then handle the exact steps safely and consistently.
whyItMatters: This is a useful design rule for business automation: give the model a narrow set of meaningful operations and keep mechanical execution outside the model. That can reduce context use, simplify testing and produce a clearer record of what the agent asked the system to do.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A simpler job gives the AI fewer chances to make mistakes. It also makes the agent’s actions easier for people to test and review.
